compiled_rows: A New World crop. Locals eat its fruit and
seeds as a staple food.
A New World vegetable whose ripe fruit turns
vivid red.
This tree grows in Southeast Asia. Its
sweet, fragrant fruit turns yellow when ripe
enough to eat.
Honeybees build this hive with care. It is
packed with nourishing nectar they gather
from flowers.
A fierce fish that sometimes attacks people.
Its fins and eggs are prized for their flavor.
Known as the king of spices, this fruit grows
on tropical plants 5 to 9 meters tall. India
produces it in abundance.
Native to Southeast Asia, cloves are dark brown
and shaped like nails. Their strong, sweet
scent comes with a tongue-numbing bite.
This tree grows from India to Southeast Asia.
Its dried bark has a distinctive sweet scent
and is used as a flavoring.
A New World chili with round or oblong fruit
that has a powerful bite when chewed.
A tree from East Africa with pure white,
jasmine-scented flowers. Its dried fruit is
roasted to make a drink.
A southern Chinese tree with long oval leaves
fermented for tea. Flavor varies by plant part
and degree of fermentation.
This tall New World tree bears large fruit
right on its trunk. The seeds are removed,
fermented, and dried for food.
A New World plant. The dried leaves are
shredded and wrapped in paper or similar
material for smoking.
A book of secrets from alchemy, the study
of what matter is made of. It explains how
to turn one substance into another.
A detailed guide to making glassware.
As these moth larvae mature, their bodies turn
clear and they spin cocoons. The silk they spin
is used to make clothing.
Worked by hand and foot, this loom weaves
fabric by interlacing threads.
This bivalve lives off Japan and produces
pearls. Its shell is almost square and
blackish brown.
An Eastern medical text of unknown authorship.
It describes how to make medicines from herbs
and bark.
A round, dark purple fruit from Southeast Asia
with juicy, delicious flesh. It's known
as the queen of fruits.
